beats.en: Long ago in France, a boy named Louis Braille was playing outside his home when he was three years old. His father was a blacksmith and was working nearby, and Louis began to play with the sharp tools around him.
beats.speakEn: Long ago in France, a boy named Louis Braille was playing outside his home when he was three years old. His father was a blacksmith and was working nearby, and Louis began to play with the sharp tools around him.

beats.en: In 1819, when Louis was ten years old, he joined the Royal Institute for Young Blind Persons in Paris. There he learnt letters by using wood, cloth or pins arranged on pincushions.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 4 english · Braille · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Braille is a method of reading by touch. Each letter is made from raised dots in a small cell of up to six dots.

beats.en: Braille is a method of reading by touch. Each letter is made from raised dots in a small cell of up to six dots. There is one Braille symbol for each of the twenty-six letters of the English alphabet.
beats.speakEn: Braille is a method of reading by touch. Each letter is made from raised dots in a small cell of up to six dots. There is one Braille symbol for each of the twenty-six letters of the English alphabet.

beats.en: A blacksmith is a person who makes things out of hot iron. Blind means unable to see. Pincushions are small soft pads where pins are stuck. Invented means made something new for the first time.
beats.speakEn: A blacksmith is a person who makes things out of hot iron. Blind means unable to see. Pincushions are small soft pads where pins are stuck. Invented means made something new for the first time.
